title: continuous-batcher-scheduler-tuning-queueing-fairness-starvation-timeouts
author: Maya Thompson
description: Motivation: Continuous batching has been the primary throughput lever for short-sequence workloads, but under mixed-priority traffic we observed starvation of QoS-sensitive requests and suboptimal tail latency when queues grew. This PR tunes the continuous-batcher scheduler to improve queueing fairness, prevent starvation, and provide configurable timeouts for partial batches. It also exposes observability hooks for per-priority queue lengths and aging metrics so SREs can detect imbalances early. Changes are gated behind a runtime feature flag (continuous_batcher.scheduler_v2) and rolled out via canary.
commits: Init scheduler v2: add priority buckets + queueing abstraction
Implement starvation prevention: aging-based token promotion and max-wait enforcement
Config: add per-priority timeouts and dynamic slot allocation
Tests: unit tests for scheduler logic and integration load test harness
Docs: scheduler tuning guide and rollout checklist

runtime/continuous_batcher/config.py - added per-priority timeouts and defaults
runtime/continuous_batcher/tests/test_scheduler_v2.py - unit tests for fairness and timeouts
runtime/continuous_batcher/load_tests/sim_mixed_priority.py - synthetic workload to validate p95/p99 behavior

review_comments: Ethan Wang: Please clarify the guarantees under bursty traffic—how does priority promotion avoid amplifying head-of-line blocking?
Maya Thompson: Reply: promotion is bounded by a max_promotion_per_interval and only moves a small token fraction to avoid HO blocking; described in scheduler_v2 docs and implemented as config knobs.
Priya Rao: Can you add a safety valve to prevent low-priority floods from starving control plane requests?
Maya Thompson: Added explicit reserved slots for control-plane and critical routes + unit test covering control-plane reservation.
Liam O'Connor: CI flakes on integration load test observed; suggest running canary on small pool first.
Maya Thompson: Increased test determinism, added retry logic, and added canary rollout notes in docs.
ci_checks: Integration load tests: pass (2/2 canary runs)
Performance benchmark job: pass (p95 under target for mixed workload)
benchmark_summary: Local cluster mixed-priority synthetic workload: before -> after: throughput +4.5% at same CPU/GPU utilization, p95 latency for high-priority requests improved from 220ms to 150ms under 80% load, starvation_events reduced from observed 18/hr to 0 in 12-hour sustained run. Tail (p99) unchanged for low-priority classes. See docs/continuous_batcher.md for full suite numbers.
rollout_plan: Ship behind feature flag continuous_batcher.scheduler_v2. Steps: 1) enable on ci/integration, 2) canary on 5% of fleet with monitoring alerts for starvation_events and wait_time_p95, 3) 25% pool after 24h if no regressions, 4) full rollout with gradual ramp and fallback to scheduler_v1 on alert. Include rollback playbook and migration notes for persisted queue state.
testing: Added unit tests for promotion logic, timeout enforcement, and reserved-slot behavior. Integration harness adds mixed-priority synthetic workload and assertions for p95/p99 and starvation events. CI matrix includes two additional runs to catch flakiness; load tests are tagged to run on nightly for longitudinal stability.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: scheduler changes could introduce head-of-line blocking if promotion misconfigured. Mitigations: default config uses conservative promotion caps, reserved slots for control plane, and an automatic fallback that disables scheduler_v2 if starvation_events increase above threshold. Also added extensive observability and alerts.
release_notes: Improved continuous-batcher scheduler: better fairness across priorities, starvation prevention via aging/promotion, configurable per-priority timeouts, and new metrics (queue_length, starvation_events, wait_time_p95). Default remains off; enable via feature flag for controlled rollout.
notes_for_ops: Ops: monitor continuous_batcher.queue_length{priority=*}, continuous_batcher.wait_time_p95, and continuous_batcher.starvation_events. Default timeouts: high=30ms, medium=60ms, low=120ms; adjust conservatively. Run canary for 24 hours and validate no increase in control-plane tail latencies.
